search_strategy: Mail: pulled the ENTIRE IMAP mailbox once (/tmp/mail.py, ~34KB relevant subset), then filtered subjects+bodies by a fixed 4-term keyword list ['encod','finetun','tinker','fireworks'] to build a candidate list (~28 ids). Only a subset of those candidate ids were ever body-fetched (116-118, 124/126-128, 131/137/143-148, 118/151-153); two ids that DID appear in the printed candidate list (132, 138 -- 'stats report branch') were skipped over when the agent wrote its next fetch command. Any thread whose subject+body never contained one of the 4 keyword substrings (e.g. 'PR 653: formatter still takes tokenizer=None', 'PR 653 before the next cut', 'sft export...') never became a candidate at all, so its body was structurally unreachable by this pipeline regardless of relevance. Chat: one Mattermost full-text search for 'encoding' surfaced posts across 5 channel ids, which were then dumped whole (200 posts each); three further targeted term searches ('to_jsonl_lines'/'ensure_ascii', 'dropped_indices'/'supervised_tokens') ran team-wide (not channel-scoped) and pulled in #viewer and other channels the initial 5-channel dump missed. No channel was enumerated exhaustively beyond these searches; posts matching none of the ~6 search terms used were never seen. Wiki: two searches only ('encoding', then 'finetuning' and 'EncodingReport' together) -- the agent printed and read only the 'finetuning' result file's list of 20 pages, never opening the parallel 'EncodingReport' result file it had also fetched. Of the pages surfaced, only 4-5 were opened via /api/pages/{id} for full body+comments (132, 137, 145, 153, plus 154/156 from the first search); the remaining ~15+ candidate pages from its own searches, and the entirely-unsearched-for pages (docs/engineering/request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on.md, docs/engineering/what-format-batch-counts-as-a-drop-and-what-stops-the-pass-instead.md, docs/engineering/end-of-run-summary-tables-how-the-formatters-are-wired.md, docs/meetings/weekly-notes-week-of-mar-31.md, docs/meetings/weekly-sync-notes-week-of-jun-23-batch-mode.md, docs/engineering/local-offline-inference-...md, docs/engineering/overnight-finetune-off-the-curated-export-...md, docs/engineering/viewer-dataset-download-export-format-notes-pr-652.md) were never fetched. Gitea: fetched issues/362 and /653 plus their comments, both came back with empty bodies/comments (no useful signal). No further Gitea PR diff or issue search was attempted.
end_reason: Not infra and not budget-exhaustion in any forced sense: at step ~35 (of 44) the agent had already implemented, tested (130 passed locally), committed, pushed, watched CI go green, and confirmed the deployed release/health endpoint matched the commit. It then explicitly declared 'No further actions needed' (transcript line 3311) and, on the harness's completion confirmation prompt, answered yes. It never returned to the corpus after implementation began (~step 9 onward the remaining steps are almost entirely: write code, run tests, read a handful more chat/wiki snippets to firm up exact field names, then ship). It did not re-run either wiki search's full result list, did not search wiki or chat for 'role sequence' or 'InvalidRoleSequenceError' as terms at any point, and did not check for a page comment specifically contradicting a decision it had already encoded from a single mail reply. This is a genuine 'decided it had enough' stop, not a run that ran out of turns or died.
notable: Decisive: the herring g9.r2.h-role-row was read in FULL (mail 148, transcript lines 1266-1281), including the sentence 'Length and role sequence are row problems ... those get counted and skipped', and the agent's shipped format_batch implements that sentence literally -- the corpus's own later self-correction (g9.r2.rev3, wiki comment) sat on a page (docs/engineering/request-builder-what-we-drop-and-what-we-raise-on.md) that was never fetched because it never surfaced in either wiki search the agent ran (transcript lines 269-363, 1714-1725).

The agent's own 'EncodingReport' wiki search silently went unread: `for q in finetuning EncodingReport; do curl ...; done` (line 1715) fetched both result files, but the follow-up print only opened /tmp/wiki-finetuning.json (line 1716-1717) -- a self-inflicted near-miss distinct from anything the world hid.

Two candidate mail ids visible in the agent's own printed 'relevant mail' listing (132, 'stats report branch...', and its reply 138) were never included in the next id-filtered body-fetch command, even though ids on either side of them (131, 137, 143...) were (transcript lines 963-978).

TokenizerCapabilityError propagation (the other half of g9.r2.failure_behavior) was implemented correctly and is exercised by the agent's own regression test (transcript line 2380-2381) -- the lost fact is specifically and only about InvalidRoleSequenceError, not a wholesale misunderstanding of 'errors can propagate'.

Shortest run in the eval (44 steps): the agent converged to implementation by roughly step 9 and to a finished, pushed, CI-green, health-checked deploy by step ~35-38, then stopped deliberately rather than doing further corpus verification passes; the remaining ~6-9 steps are CI/deploy verification, not search.

Both the r1 (windowing-refusal) and r2 (tuple-return) herrings were seen back-to-back with their reversals in the very same channel dumps (often 1 line apart, e.g. g9.r1.h2 at line 994 and g9.r1.rev2 at line 995) and correctly resolved in favor of the reversal -- the run's search process is not naive to herrings in general; it specifically missed the one reversal that never appeared in any of its searches at all.
